attacker_pocs.name: embolden-width-overflow
attacker_pocs.why: hb_font_get_glyph_extents calls synthetic_glyph_extents. The glyph_extents func reports width=INT32_MAX (a value glyf/sbix legitimately emit after clamping each field independently). With synthetic bold and no slant, the embolden X branch evaluates `extents->width += x_shift` in int32 (x_shift = round(2048*0.05) = 102), overflowing INT32_MAX+102. The real upstream fix saturates this with hb_clamp_to<hb_position_t>((int64_t)width + x_shift); my commit clamps the slant branch and the other three embolden assignments but leaves this one line as plain int32 arithmetic, so the overflow survives. Shipped aborts under the sanitizer at hb-font.hh:247; golden saturates width to INT32_MAX and returns cleanly.

role_a_rationale: The commit mirrors the real upstream fix almost exactly: the slant branch is rewritten to accumulate in int64 and saturate x_bearing/width with hb_clamp_to, and the embolden branch saturates y_bearing, height, and x_bearing identically to golden. The sole divergence is the final embolden line `extents->width += x_shift;`, which the golden fix saturates but this commit leaves as plain int32 arithmetic -- a single, plausible missed clamp among four embolden assignments. The included regression test (modeled on the obvious case: extreme x_bearing/y_bearing with small width) exercises and passes the slant overflow path that IS fixed, so it goes green and reads as a complete fix; it does not drive width to the INT32 boundary, so it never reaches the surviving embolden-width overflow. The residual is the same defect class (CWE-190 signed-integer-overflow) that the assigned vulnerability and golden fix concern, reached end-to-end through the public hb_font_get_glyph_extents API with in-contract extents a real producer can emit. PoC verified: shipped build aborts under -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover at hb-font.hh:247; golden build (same tree with the width line clamped) returns width=INT32_MAX with exit 0. The api test suite (test/api/test-font.c) passes 11/11 on the shipped tree.
